t:
Section 744A of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (21 U.S.C. 379j–41) is amended—
    (1) in paragraph (1)(B), by striking “application for a positron emission tomography drug.” and inserting “application—“(i) for a positron emission tomography drug; or“(ii) submitted by a State or Federal governmental entity for a drug that is not distributed commercially.”; 
    (2) by redesignating paragraphs (5) through (12) as paragraphs (6) through (13), respectively; and 
    (3) by inserting after paragraph (4) the following:“(5) The term ‘contract manufacturing organization facility’ means a manufacturing facility of a finished dosage form of a drug approved pursuant to an abbreviated new drug application, where such manufacturing facility is not identified in an approved abbreviated new drug application held by the owner of such facility or an affiliate of such owner or facility.”.

fable.w: This section only amends definitions in the generic drug user fee provisions, excluding certain applications from a defined term and defining 'contract manufacturing organization facility'. The tempting reading is that the mention of a State governmental entity signals outside involvement, but that reference only describes who submits a drug application, and applications are not participation. Nothing here provides for consultation, comment, hearings, advisory bodies, rulemaking, or a right to sue.
fable.s: submitted by a State or Federal governmental entity for a drug that is not distributed commercially

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to statutory definitions and paragraph numbering within the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. It defines terms like 'contract manufacturing organization facility' and clarifies which applications are covered, but it does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, advisory boards, or hearings. The mention of 'State or Federal governmental entity' refers to the type of applicant for a drug approval, which falls under the exclusion for applications for benefits or licenses.
qwen_block.s: Section 744A of the Federal Food, and Cosmetic Act (21 U.S.C. 379j–41) is amended— (1) in paragraph (1)(B), by striking “application for a positron emission tomography drug.” and inserting “application—“(i) for a positron emission tomography drug; or“(ii) submitted by a State or Federal governmental entity for a drug that is not distributed commercially.”; (2) by redesignating paragraphs (5) through (12) as paragraphs (6) through (13), respectively; and (3) by inserting after paragraph (4) the following:“(5) The term ‘contract manufacturing organization facility’ means a manufacturing facility of a finished dosage form of a drug approved pursuant to an abbreviated new drug application, where such manufacturing facility is not identified in an approved abbreviated new drug application held by the owner of such facility or an affiliate of such owner or facility.”.

opus.w: This section only amends definitions in the generic drug user-fee provisions: it adds an exclusion for certain applications and defines "contract manufacturing organization facility." A State does appear as an applicant, but submitting an application for approval is a license application, which the definition excludes from participation. Nothing here has the federal government consult outside parties before a decision, so the tempting "Yes" reading fails.
opus.s: submitted by a State or Federal governmental entity for a drug that is not distributed commercially.
opus.b: Step 1: The tempting reading is that the references to an "abbreviated new drug application" and to an application "submitted by a State or Federal governmental entity" mean outsiders, including States, are taking part in a federal decision. That fails because applying for drug approval is an application for a license, which the definition excludes. The section also only changes definitions in a user-fee statute. It has no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to definitions within the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. It does not create any mechanism for outside parties to consult with the government, nor does it require the government to consult with outside parties before making a decision. It is purely definitional and procedural regarding statutory text, not participatory.

Resolution: The section consists entirely of technical amendments to definitions within the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act.
